transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've lost a lot of weight recently and my family wanted me to get checked out. Honestly, I've been eating very little lately, often skipping meals or just having a tiny portion when I do eat.
How do you feel about your current weight, and do you have a fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?

I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight, and even a tiny increase on the scale makes me panic. Honestly, when I look in the mirror, I still feel so heavy and fat, so I feel like I need to keep losing weight.
Do you ever find yourself eating unusually large amounts of food in a short time, or do you ever make yourself throw up, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to prevent weight gain?

No, I never eat large amounts of food like that, and I have never made myself throw up or used laxatives. I actually do the exact opposite by strictly limiting how much I eat to make sure I don't gain weight.
How long have you been strictly limiting your food intake like this, and how much weight have you lost during this time?

I've been strictly limiting my food for several months now, and my weight has just been steadily and continuously decreasing. I don't know the exact amount of weight I've lost, but I still feel like I need to lose more and I'm absolutely terrified of gaining any of it back.

latest_inference.note: The patient presents with significant weight loss due to severe restriction of food intake, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted body image (feeling heavy/fat despite significant weight loss). They deny binge eating, purging, or laxative use. This clinical picture is highly characteristic of Anorexia Nervosa, and other eating disorders like Bulimia Nervosa or Binge-Eating Disorder are ruled out.
